findings.title: forEach with async callback: promises are fire-and-forget, try/catch is ineffective
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` does not await the async callbacks. The surrounding `try/catch` on line 124 will never catch errors thrown inside the async callback because `forEach` returns `undefined`, not a Promise. Additionally, the function may return `true` (line 151) and send the reschedule email before calendar/video events are actually deleted. Use `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))` instead.

findings.title: forEach with async callback: promises are fire-and-forget, try/catch is ineffective
findings.body: Same issue as vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` does not await the async callbacks. The surrounding try/catch will never catch rejections from `getCalendar` or `deleteMeeting`, and the function proceeds to send emails before deletions complete. Use `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` instead.

findings.title: forEach with async callback: calendar/video deletions are not awaited
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` fires async callbacks without awaiting them. The `getCalendar` and `deleteMeeting` calls inside will produce unhandled promise rejections on failure, and the mutation handler will return before the calendar/video events are actually deleted. This can leave stale events on users' calendars after a reschedule. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` instead.

findings.title: forEach with async callback: apiDeletes array may be empty when consumed
findings.body: Inside the recurring-event branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => {...})` pushes results into `apiDeletes` from async callbacks that are never awaited. By the time `apiDeletes` is consumed at line 617 (`await apiDeletes`) or line 652 (`await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`), the array may still be empty because the forEach callbacks haven't finished. This means calendar events for recurring bookings may never be deleted. Replace with a `for...of` loop or `Promise.all(...map(...))` and collect the promises properly.

findings.title: Sequential await in loop where parallel loading is possible
findings.body: `getVideoAdapters` now uses a `for...of` loop with `await appStore[appName]` inside, loading each video app module sequentially. Previously all app lookups were synchronous. Since each `import()` is independent, they could be loaded in parallel with `Promise.all(withCredentials.map(...))` to avoid unnecessary sequential latency, especially when multiple video credentials are present.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials returns objects with unresolved Promise in calendar field
findings.body: `getCalendar` is now async but `getCalendarCredentials` is synchronous and stores the returned Promise directly in the `calendar` property without awaiting it. While `getConnectedCalendars` correctly does `await item.calendar`, any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` that accesses `.calendar` expecting a `Calendar | null` will get a Promise instead. The return type of `getCalendarCredentials` should be updated to reflect that `calendar` is `Promise<Calendar | null>`, or the function should be made async.
